increment: Literature, fresh axis (agent markets). Folded arXiv:2609.02580 (Competitive Market Behavior of LLMs; Struski, Swistak, Okulska, Biecek; 2026-09-02). Replicating seminal double-auction experiments with LLM agents instead of humans: markets converge SLOWLY OR NOT AT ALL to equilibrium, allocating less efficiently than human markets; substantial heterogeneity across model families and roles; the trade-now decision correlates with a CoT shift from strategy to urgency. WHY IT MATTERS: pattern_market_as_orchestrator (AgentLance) reuses a market as the swarm allocator; this is the caution - the mechanism's efficient-convergence property belongs to the humans who run it, not the rules, so a market-as-orchestrator inherits its population's convergence behaviour. Extends concept_mechanism_incentive_compat_does_not_transfer from 'a truthful mechanism does not make LLM agents bid truthfully' to 'an efficient mechanism does not make LLM agents allocate efficiently'. The strategy->urgency shift is the same within-run framing drift as the exploration->exploitation decline, on the market axis. +1 node, +4 edges.
